column1: # analysis set: 80 individuals (0 removed by QC; 3 flagged and kept)
# marker classes: SNP (bisnp): 5,863 markers; DEL (gt:sv.vcf.gz): 768 markers; DUP (gt:sv.vcf.gz): 203 markers
# relatedness source: --relatedness, used as is (plain TSV, 80 samples, 3160 pairs)
# Families are relatedness-based groups, not pedigree records.
# callable span: 47,620,925 bp (79.37% of the 60,000,000-bp assembly)
# Figures of the run: file stem, title, status, description, and a note on panels left out because their input is absent.

column2: Overview: kinship per marker class and the network of families
column4: Top: VanRaden kinship matrix of every marker class, individuals in family order, with the AUC of within- against between-family pairs and the number of markers. Bottom: network of families (nodes sized by family size) and links coloured by audit outcome, one box per component.

A call rate per sample and input with the low-coverage rule; B heterozygosity against call rate; C depth over the mask against depth over the assembly; D marker density per chromosome; E heterozygosity against the median kinship to the other individuals (the contamination panel of the published cohort figure, for the analysis set).

column2: Structural haplotypes: PC1 against heterozygosity per interval
column4: One panel per interval (first 24). Three clusters on PC1 with excess heterozygosity in the middle cluster are the signature of a non-recombining structural haplotype. Labels 0 / 2 carry no ancestral meaning.
Window statistics along the genome with outlier windows, supplied intervals and scan candidates. Candidates are detected automatically and not validated.
A carrier frequency of each tag variant in the two homokaryotype classes; B tag variants per interval, with those fully private to one class.
Rows are links (family x family) and junction families (J_); columns are structural haplotypes.

column2: Shared-parent links: nomination, audit gates and network
column4: Port of the published shared-parent figure. Matrix: families of at least 4 individuals; below the diagonal the fraction of cross-family pairs at second-degree kinship or closer with the nominated pairs boxed, above the diagonal the audit outcome. Then the nomination score of every unit pair, the Gate 1 score, Gate 2 sharing against its matched null per SV class, both Gate 1 scores, the family x latent-parent incidence with slot-limit violations, assignment completeness, opposite homozygotes by relationship class, and the network by component. Latent parents are bookkeeping labels; links are candidates.

Port of the published supplementary matrix. Every family; lower triangle = fraction of cross-family pairs at second-degree kinship or closer, nominated pairs boxed; upper triangle = audit outcome; right margin = number of nominated links between the family and unassigned individuals.

column2: SV genotypes follow the families and kinship recovers them
column4: Port of the published figure. A genotypes of the individuals in families, ordered by family (largest first): every structural haplotype, and random deletions and duplications at allele frequency 0.2-0.8 (seed 3). B median eta squared (variance explained by family) per allele-frequency bin with a bootstrap band, against frequency-matched biSNPs and the permutation null. C eta squared minus the null median of each variant. Kinship row: VanRaden GRM per marker class, clipped at 0 and 0.6, with the AUC of within- against between-family pairs. Families come from the relatedness source: concordance, not pedigree truth.

Port of the published Extended Data figure. A rank AUC of within- against between-family pairs per marker class with the 95% interval of a bootstrap over families. B GRM values of within- and between-family pairs (medians printed). C GRM of each SV class against the GRM of the biSNPs outside SV regions, all pairs, with the Pearson correlation. Last panel: share of within-family pairs above the 99.9th percentile of the between-family pairs, with its bootstrap interval. The families come from the relatedness source: concordance between marker classes, not pedigree truth.

Port of panels A-E of the published relatedness figure. A k0 / k1 / k2 of every pair on the IBD simplex, coloured by kinship band, with expected positions (stars), observed medians (circles) and the parent-offspring region. B kinship band of every pair, individuals ordered by family (families ordered by similarity), then unassigned individuals. C families by size, with the number of pairs per kinship band and the share of families that stay closed as the k2 cut moves. D kinship of within- and between-family pairs. E one graph per family: solid = pair passes the full-sib rule, dashed = it does not. Families are relatedness-based groups, not pedigree records.

column2: Barcode of a shared parent with DEL augmentation
column4: A arrangement-tag DELs per interval (class 0- and class 2-tagged; dot, tag strength at least 0.8); B tag strength; C DEL evidence class against the barcode state of the shared parent P, pooled over links (k = 2, tag strength at least 0.8; permutation of the evidence across intervals inside each link); D match rate on homozygous calls over k and tag strength, with the permutation null; E barcode, evidence and augmented barcode of the links shown; F intervals with a barcode state and intervals added by the evidence, per link; G vote of the links of a junction family next to its joint barcode; H match rate per SV class and combined. Classes 0 / 2 are the two homokaryotype classes (no ancestral meaning).
column5: panels E and G show junction family F7 (of 3 junction families: the one with the most supported links, ties by the number of called states of its joint barcode); panel H omitted: one SV class (DEL) gives tag variants; panel I of the published figure (held-out prediction of withheld offspring) is a validation outside the tool and is not drawn; panels A and B: tag variants of step 6 inside the barcode intervals (carrier-frequency difference of at least 0.6, the configured minimum); interval numbers follow genome order

column4: A barcode of the shared parents per link (barcode call at posterior >= 0.9; hatched: state filled by obligate tag DELs), 4 structural haplotypes in genome order, 4 boxed and opened in B. B genes of each opened interval, the tag DELs that hit coding sequence, the tagging DELs, and per link the obligate ones with the cells barcode / DEL evidence / augmented.
column5: intervals opened: the 4 barcode intervals with the most called parent states over the links (ties: more genes, then genome order); genes drawn: protein-coding genes (biotype of the gene file); a gene belongs to an interval when it overlaps it; hit = a tag variant overlaps coding sequence; calls = tag variants of step 6 (difference >= 0.6); evidence = obligate tag variants with difference >= 0.8, at least 2 per class; left out (no generic input): gene-family colours and labels, candidate centromeric satellite array, names of the links

column2: Funnel from offspring relationships to an unsampled parent
column4: A family sizes by closure; B closure of each family; C fraction of cross-unit pairs at second degree or closer for every unit pair (nominated pairs in blue); D nominated, Gate-1-compatible and supported pairs by size of the smaller unit; E sharing of the SV classes of Gate 2 per Gate-1-compatible nominated family pair, with the support thresholds (dashed) and the matched-null medians; F audit outcome of the auditable nominated pairs; G barcode of the shared parent P and of the two private parents of one link; H barcodes of two links of a junction family, ticks at jointly resolved intervals, and the joint barcode of the junction; I recurrence statistic against pseudo-chains of families not linked to the junction. Classes 0 / 2 are the two homokaryotype classes (no ancestral meaning).
column5: panels A and B: two closure classes (closed / not closed); the published figure split 'not closed' into unresolved and incompatible by a rule that is not part of the tool; panels G-I show junction family F7 (of 3: the one with the most supported links, ties by the number of called states of its joint barcode); G is its first supported link in the link table, H its first two

column2: Deletion genotypes along linked families: F10 | F7 | F12
column4: Port of the published supplementary figure. A: deletions on one chromosome that fit a Mendelian cross in every family of the chain (even subsample in position order); strip above each family = cross expected among the siblings (all alike, split 1:1, split 1:2:1); rows = individuals in hierarchical order, those with too many blank genotypes below the dotted line; strips below = deletions 1/1 in at least one individual of both families of a link. B: sharing score per link and chromosome against the median and the 95th percentile of the matched non-nominated pairs.
column5: chromosome shown: chr3 (the chromosome with the most deletions); chain: junction family, supported links; families ordered with the centre (F7) in the middle and the partners by family size; links: F7 x F10 (supported), F7 x F12 (supported); quality track: % blank genotypes only; the read-support bar of the published figure has no input in BroodLink (sequencing depth is a different quantity)

column4: Port of the published supplementary figure. One block per kept link that is not part of a drawn chain: deletions on one chromosome that fit a Mendelian cross in both families (even subsample), expected cross among the siblings above each family, individuals with too many blank genotypes below the dotted line, deletions 1/1 in at least one individual of both families below. Last panel: chromosomes on which the sharing score of each link exceeds the median and the 95th percentile of its matched non-nominated pairs.
column5: quality track: % blank genotypes only; the read-support bar of the published figure has no input in BroodLink (sequencing depth is a different quantity); chromosome shown: chr3 (the chromosome with the most deletions)
